 World Live updates: Democrats show early strength; Trump takes aim at Fox News and voter poll
 A pivotal US midterm election is underway. Follow live as results come in and the battle for Congress takes shape. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are in play at these elections, as are 35 seats in the Senate. Source: Getty / Kevin Dietsch Published 4 November 2026 6:00am 
 Updated 3m ago 12:33pm 
 By Jack Revell , Ben Lewis , Madeleine Wedesweiler , David Aidone
 Source : SBS News
 Skip to live blog content Tags
 United States 
 Share this with family and friends
 Copy link Share PINNED 11:01am , 2h ago Watch live coverage of the US midterm elections
 Disclaimer: This livestream is from SBS News' US partner broadcaster PBS and the material broadcast may not reflect SBS' editorial standards. The SBS Code of Practice does not apply to the PBS content within this program 
 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT 12:28pm , 8m ago Looking ahead to 2028
 While it’s all about the House and the Senate, I’m also keeping an eye on some of the gubernatorial (great word) races, as several Governors are likely to enter the race to become the Democrats' 2028 Presidential candidate.  
 There have been easy wins for Josh Shapiro in Pennsylvania, JB Pritzker in Illinois and Wes Moore in Maryland. 
 The newly re-elected senator for Georgia Jon Ossoff is another possibility, given he has registered impressive numbers in what has become a Presidential swing state. 
 — Ben Lewis 
 12:19pm , 16m ago Has redrawing the map backfired?
 In the lead-up to the midterms, several Republican states (then, in turn, several Democratic states) engaged in redistricting — well, gerrymandering — to try to shore up seats by moving electoral boundaries. 
 US laws allow for the practice, and it ramped up in several states ahead of the midterms with many electoral maps redrawn. 
 In Florida, there are early signs it's backfired. 
 Take the 14 th district, which Republicans redrew to put the party 11 points ahead. 
 READ MORE
 'Race to the bottom': Donald Trump, the midterm elections, and a battle over maps 
 Now, it looks like Democratic incumbent Kathy Castor is going to win it by a six-point margin. 
 It could be an example of what some call "dummymandering". 
 — Ben Lewis 
 12:11pm , 24m ago Democrats looking strong as more results come in
 Early results have continued to trickle in, with very preliminary indications of a strong performance for the Democrats. 
 Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff has held his Senate seat in Georgia. 
 Some 18 seats in the House have been called for the Democrats, while 9 have been called for the Republicans. Two Senate seats have been called for the Democrats. 
 While many of these results are for safe races, the swings seen in some areas have Republicans concerned. 
 In Florida's 13th Congressional District, for example, the Republican incumbent leads by just 0.2 per cent, with 95 per cent of the vote counted — in an area Trump carried by 13 points at the last election. 
 In Anderson County, Kentucky, the Republican incumbent is 20 points down on the 2024 results. 
 Ossoff is current beating his opponent, Mike Collins , by 25 points at 37 per cent of the vote counted. 
 — Jack Revell 
 12:09pm , 27m ago 'The worst vote I ever cast': Two years of frustration
 United States President Donald Trump has asked voters to treat the midterm elections as a referendum on his presidency . 
 Some voters my colleague Alexandra Jones spoke to in Arizona say the first two years of Trump's second term have made them question their choices, as broken promises pile up. 
 Even in conservative strongholds, frustration with Trump is top of mind. 
 You can watch the full report here: 
 — Madeleine Wedesweiler 
 11:48am , 47m ago What else have Americans voted on?
 For millions of Americans, senators and representatives weren't the only thing on their ballots. 
 SBS News' Veronica Lenard has taken a look what else they've had their say on, from abortion rights to tax reform. 
 READ MORE
 It's not just Congress: What else have Americans voted on in the midterms? 
 11:46am , 50m ago Trump lashes out as early results trickle in
 Donald Trump has expressed his frustration with Fox News — a US channel traditionally warm toward the president and his Republican allies — for covering the US media-backed Voter Poll. 
 The poll, which we posted about below, surveys tens of thousands of Americans and includes exit poll sentiments. It was commissioned by a wide array of media networks, including Fox. 
 "The FoxNews Poll, always the worst, is so insulting with the questions they ask," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Every question is a hit job, and every answer is "BULLSHIT!" This has been going on for years." 
 READ MORE
 As Americans vote, these are the key battlegrounds that could decide Trump's future 
 In a separate post on the social media platform he owns, Trump again lashed out at the station, claiming that its recent ratings declines are because Fox has spent "too much time covering the Trump Deranged Dumbocrats!" and not him. 
 "All of those people who used to watch Fox, and no longer do, get it. It's them, not me — My numbers are better than they have ever been," wrote Trump, whose approval ratings are at a historic low. 
 He also questioned why the network would spend so much time covering his rivals in the Democratic Party and elsewhere. 
 Earlier, Trump's final pitch to voters was mostly about the Reflecting Pool makeover. 
 You can watch that full report here: 
 — Jack Revell 
 11:39am , 57m ago How were Republicans polling in the lead-up to the midterms?
 Polls can be wrong, and they often are. 
 But if they're right, there's very little chance of the Republicans holding both the Senate and the House. 
 Many pollsters have given the Democrats the edge in a number of Senate and Congressional races — even in some of the country's reddest states. 
 My colleague Ben Lewis says it would be "apocalyptic" for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton to lose to James Talarico in Texas, but it could happen. 
 You can watch more on that here: 
 — Madeleine Wedesweiler 
 11:17am , 1h ago First results come in
 The first results of the 2026 midterms have been announced in Virginia, Florida, and Kentucky. 
 Democrat Mark R Warner has held his seat in Virginia — winning a fourth term against Republican challenger Bert Mizusawa. 
 In the House of Representatives, two of six races in Kentucky have been called, with the Republicans and Democrats claiming a seat each. 
 In Florida, Democrats have so far won two House seats. 
 — Jack Revell 
 11:16am , 1h ago Where could the midterms be won or lost?
 While United States President Donald Trump's brand is thought to be toxic for the Republicans , a blue wave in this year's midterms is far from guaranteed. 
 In the House of Representatives, Democrats are predicted to pick up 21 seats — enough to secure majority control of that chamber. 
 Taking control of the Senate may be harder, with fewer opportunities for Democrats to flip Republican-held seats. 
 However, the Republicans are at risk of losing a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in decades, with polling showing Ken Paxton behind young progressive James Talarico . 
 Watch the full report from my colleague Liz Maddock here: 
 — Madeleine Wedesweiler 
 11:03am , 2h ago How will gen Z be voting?
 The major issues at stake in this year's midterms may push more gen Z Americans than usual to cast a vote, experts say. 
 Young people in Arizona, interviewed by my colleague Alexandra Jones, said the economy, cost of living, and the job market are all top of mind. 
 They're also concerned about the war with Iran and the release of the Epstein files. 
 Research shows young men are more likely to vote conservative, while young women are on average more progressive. 
 You can watch the full interviews here: 
 — Madeleine Wedesweiler 
 11:00am , 2h ago More polls close
 A second tranche of polls have shut in the US. 
 Doors have closed across the entirety of Indiana, Kentucky, Vermont, Virginia, South Carolina, and Georgia. 
 Those latter three states tend to complete all their counts on election night. 
 It took the Associated Press six hours to call the winner in the earliest of the three, Georgia, at the 2024 presidential election. 
 Polls have also closed in parts of Florida and New Hampshire. 
 Results from those states that have fully stopped receiving ballots should begin to come in shortly. 
 — Jack Revell 
 10:55am , 2h ago Voters cast their ballots
 With polling still open across much of the country, millions of Americans are still diligently filling out ballot cards or lining up at polling stations. 
 Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at the Baker Center in Austin, Texas. Source: AFP,Getty / Chip Somodevilla A man walks into the Valley Bible Chalet to cast his ballot in Indian, Alaska. Source: AAP,AP / Lindsey Wasson People stand in line to vote near official election signage in English and Spanish, at a polling place in West Palm Beach, Florida. Source: AP,AAP / Rebecca Blackwell Residents vote at a polling station in Saint Timothy's Episcopal Church in West Des Moines, Iowa. Source: AFP,Getty / Anna Moneymaker — Jack Revell 
 10:38am , 2h ago Midterms could bring a wave of historic firsts
 Featuring one of the most diverse slates of both Democratic and Republican candidates in recent years, this midterm election has set up a possible wave of historic leadership firsts across the country. 
 Voters could propel into office the first Native American female governor and Native women senators, the first Black female governor, the first openly gay male US senator and the first Muslim US senator , among other milestones. Most are Democrats, but the GOP could also break ground. 
 While some of these candidates have avoided focusing on the inherent historic value of their race, gender, religion or sexual orientation, some voters' rights advocates are celebrating how the electorate has expanded. 
 "These firsts show how our country is changing," said Alexis Anderson-Reed , president and CEO of State Voices, a network of advocates for civic engagement and equity in democracy, via an email. 
 "For years, people of colour and LGBTQ+ communities have organised, knocked on doors, talked to voters, held conversations, and done the hard work of saving our democracy," Anderson-Reed said. "These wins are because of them." 
 — Associated Press 
 10:31am , 2h ago The state of play so far
 As we eagerly await the first results to start trickling in — expected at 11am AEST — let's take a look at where things stand so far. 
 All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are in play at these elections, as are 35 seats in the Senate. 
 However, due to political polarisation and gerrymandering , not all of those are expected to be tight contests. 
 Roughly 53 House seats are thought to be competitive, according to the Cook Political Report, with the remaining 382 considered safe for one party or the other. 
 The same is true of the Senate, where six seats are considered a toss-up, while three lean Democrat and two lean Republican. 
 — Jack Revell 
 10:07am , 2h ago National voter poll reveals top election issues
 A major survey incorporating exit poll sentiments has revealed voters' top concerns when casting their ballots. 
 The economy ranked first in The Voter Poll — commissioned by several major US news outlets and carried out by pollster SSRS — which surveys tens of thousands of Americans. 
 The state of democracy was number two, while immigration was a distant third. 
 The polls may indicate trouble for the Republicans, who have tried to avoid mentioning the cost of living during campaigning. Democrats have made it a key message. 
 — Jack Revell 
 10:02am , 3h ago The first polls have closed in the US
 Voting in most of Indiana and Kentucky has now wrapped up. 
 The results from those states will not be known until all polling stations close, which will happen in the next hour. 
 Indiana's 5th congressional district and Kentucky's 6th are ones to watch, as they could be close contests and early indicators of where the day might go. 
 Polls will begin shutting across a wider swathe of states at 11am AEST as Vermont, Virginia, South Carolina, Georgia and most of Florida close shop. 
 Some parts of New Hampshire will also close their polls, as well as the remaining counties in Indiana and Kentucky. 
 — Jack Revell 
 9:58am , 3h ago 'Remarkably' few issues affecting voting
 Voting so far has unfolded with relatively few problems. 
 By the afternoon, the biggest issues affecting voting were weather-related, with flooding in Florida and parts of the Southwest prompting changes to polling locations and other emergency measures. 
 A problem with ballot scanners also delayed vote counting — though voting was able to continue — in New York's suburban Westchester County, part of which is in a US House district with a competitive race. 
 Ballots were to be placed in emergency bags for later counting. Officials stressed that the ballots would remain secure and monitored and that voters could continue casting ballots while they worked to resolve the issue. 
 Hannah Fried, CEO of the voting rights group All Voting Is Local, said the issues she's seen are "garden-variety stuff that any of us who works on elections is used to seeing, and it's quickly resolved". 
 David Becker, executive director of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, said it was "remarkable" to have so few issues, and suggested the massive early voting turnout may have contributed to a smoother Election Day. 
 — Associated Press 
 9:54am , 3h ago What's on the minds of voters?
 President Donald Trump has repeatedly encouraged voters to pretend he's on the ballot this Election Day . 
 He's not, of course. But there's reason to believe that this year's midterms, above all, will be a referendum on his performance over the last two years. 
 History, polling and early voting numbers suggest it could be a difficult night for Trump's Republican Party. 
 Voters are in the mood for change, according to the Associated Press Voter Poll, which found that roughly three-quarters of voters say they feel "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the way things are going in the country today. 
 Most appear to blame the Trump administration for high costs. About 6 in 10 say higher than usual prices are "more because of Trump's policies" rather than "more because of factors outside Trump's control". 
 — Associated Press 
 9:53am , 3h ago Department of Justice sends election monitors overwhelmingly to Democratic areas
 The US Justice Department has deployed "the largest monitoring effort in DOJ history" at these elections, sending 1,000 election officials to verify the counts. 
 The DOJ has sent monitors to all 50 states, but two-thirds of those deployed have been dispatched to areas won by Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. 
 The Trump administration has taken an aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. 
 President Donald Trump continues to maintain that the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to Joe Biden, was "rigged" and "stolen", without evidence. 
 — Jack Revell 
 9:40am , 3h ago Trump's historically low approval ratings ahead of polling
 United States President Donald Trump has one of the lowest approval ratings of any US president in the post-war era at this point in their term. 
 Whether the sentiment will translate into votes remains to be seen. 
 — Jack Revell
